content.overview: Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 sets the grounds of divorce. Either spouse may petition on adultery after solemnization, cruelty, desertion for a continuous period of not less than two years immediately preceding the petition, conversion so that the respondent has ceased to be a Hindu, incurable unsoundness of mind or a mental disorder of the stated kind, venereal disease in a communicable form, renunciation of the world by entering a religious order, and not being heard of as alive for seven years. Leprosy was a historical ground and was omitted by the Personal Laws (Amendment) Act, 2019; it is not pleaded as a current ground. Section 13(1A) adds non-resumption of cohabitation for one year or more after judicial separation, and no restitution of conjugal rights for one year or more after a section 9 decree. Section 13(2) gives the wife additional grounds.
content.study: Match the facts to one clause. Count desertion as two years immediately before the petition. Do not plead leprosy. Use section 13(2) only for a wife's additional ground. Use section 13B, not section 13, for mutual consent.

learningObjectives: List the section 13(1) grounds and the 2019 leprosy omission.
State the wife's additional grounds in section 13(2).
enhancement.definition: Section 13 is the contested-divorce provision: stated grounds for either spouse, two decree-based grounds, and additional grounds for the wife.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Divorce under section 13 is ground-specific. A ground not written in the section, including omitted leprosy, is not a section 13 decree.
enhancement.statutoryFramework: Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, section 13. Personal Laws (Amendment) Act, 2019, omitting the leprosy ground. Section 13B is mutual consent.
essentialIngredients: Desertion of two continuous years immediately before the petition, if that ground is used
One-year non-resumption after the earlier decree, if section 13(1A) is used
Wife's additional ground only if section 13(2) is used
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 13(1) grounds for either party are voluntary sexual intercourse with another person after solemnization, cruelty, desertion for not less than two years immediately preceding presentation, ceasing to be a Hindu by conversion, incurable unsoundness of mind or a continuing or intermittent mental disorder such that the petitioner cannot reasonably be expected to live with the respondent, venereal disease in a communicable form, renunciation by entering a religious order, and seven years not heard of as alive. The leprosy clause was omitted in 2019. Section 13(1A) lets either party petition where there has been no resumption of cohabitation for one year or upwards after a judicial-separation decree, or no restitution for one year or upwards after a section 9 decree. Section 13(2) lets the wife also petition where the husband married again before the Act or another wife was alive at the solemnization, where the husband has since the solemnization been guilty of rape, sodomy or bestiality, where a maintenance order under section 18 of the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act or section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, or the corresponding later law, has been followed by one year of non-cohabitation, or where the marriage was solemnized before she was fifteen and she repudiated it after fifteen and before eighteen. Cruelty and adultery standards are case-law and are not given a ratio here.
examples: Desertion from June 2022, petition in May 2024. The two years immediately preceding the petition are not complete.
No cohabitation for fourteen months after a judicial-separation decree. Section 13(1A) is the ground, not a fresh cruelty plea.
A wife pleads virulent leprosy. That ground was omitted and is not used.
enhancement.problemApplication: Pick the clause, check the time condition, and keep section 13(2) to a wife petitioner. Do not import section 13B consent into a contested petition.
distinctions: Section 13 contested grounds vs section 13B mutual consent
Section 13(1A) decree-based divorce vs a fresh section 9 petition
enhancement.caseLawNotes: No new case citation or ratio was added. Cooling-off waiver and cruelty tests remain on the case-law gate.
enhancement.shortAnswerStructure: Either spouse may petition on the section 13(1) grounds, or on a one-year failure after judicial separation or restitution. The wife has additional grounds. Leprosy is omitted.

keyTakeaways: Desertion must be two continuous years immediately before the petition.
Section 13(1A) needs an earlier decree and one year without resumption.
Section 13(2) is the wife's additional list.
Leprosy is not a current ground.
